envelope.summary: Every requirement (REQ-1..REQ-12) is covered by at least one task with named verification. The 8-task DAG is acyclic with contracts produced before consumers. No parallel_safe_with pair overlaps in file_scope, each leaf has an explicit contract and observable acceptance, and all future needs are hypothetical, with no speculative tasks. One low, non-blocking note concerns the order in which the rate-limit plugin and the save route are registered in TASK-03.

findings.problem: @fastify/rate-limit applies per-route limits through an onRoute hook that it adds only when the plugin loads (node_modules/@fastify/rate-limit/index.js:172). buildApp() is synchronous (src/server/app.ts:4). If TASK-03 calls registerResultsRoute(app, store) directly after app.register(rateLimit), the POST route can be declared before that hook exists, and the route-level limit would silently not apply. The planned 429 inject test would catch this, so it is a risk to implementation, not a gap in the decomposition.
findings.expected_fix: In TASK-03, register the results route inside an encapsulated app.register(...) plugin (or after the rate-limit plugin has loaded), so the onRoute hook sees the route config. Keep the 11th-save 429 inject test as the guard.
